mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the median rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered quarters, or the mechanism's median IC is not statistically significant at p<0.10.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the correlation between UNRATE and returns turns positive.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both UNRATE and PAYEMS signals a robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE and PAYEMS both increase month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically different from zero in triggered periods, or the joint proxy's predictive power (R^2) drops below 0.02.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for four consecutive months signals weakening manufacturing output and reduced corporate revenues, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism's out-of-sample Sharpe ratio is not positive.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both GDPC1 and HOUST over two consecutive months signals strengthening housing and overall demand, which boosts consumer confidence and corporate sales, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both increase month-over-month for 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly above zero in triggered periods, or the interaction term's coefficient is not statistically significant at p<0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate held below 2% for more than six consecutive months in a low-inflation environment signals accommodative monetary policy, which supports equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly positive during triggered periods, or the joint proxy's predictive power is not robust to regime shifts.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in industrial production (INDPRO) for five consecutive months signals improving manufacturing activity and higher corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not statistically greater than zero in more than 80% of triggered periods, or the mechanism's out-of-sample hit ratio falls below 0.55.
